heading: ‘A CRISIS OF AUTHENTICITY': THE TRUTH ABOUT FOOD INFLUENCERS (18 MINUTE READ)
summary: A Guardian investigation into food influencers reveals how they've become the dominant force shaping London's restaurant landscape since the early 2020s. Once operating in a free-meal-for-coverage system with restaurants and PR firms, influencers like Topjaw and Eating With Tod (Toby Inskip with 2.4 million Instagram followers) now command audiences rivaling entire print media circulations; one Inskip reel can reach more viewers than the UK's total print circulation. The algorithm's shift toward short-form video content and personality-driven posts—rather than food photography—has created a new generation of highly performative influencers, though most still lack steady income despite their reach, with under-100,000-follower accounts charging £300-600 per post and only a small fraction earning full-time income. The article documents a largely unspoken but systematic arrangement where influencers receive free meals and access in exchange for almost universally positive coverage, raising questions about undisclosed payments and authenticity; industry insiders acknowledge the quid pro quo while staying technically within loose UK advertising regulations. Critics and audiences have begun pushing back against what one influencer termed a "crisis of authenticity," noting that established influencers like Inskip face accusations of paid endorsements disguised as genuine recommendations.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: WIN REPORT: HOW SUPPLY-SIDE CRO LIFTED SIGN-UPS BY 15% (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: A private tutoring marketplace tested adding a real student job posting to their tutor recruitment landing page, replacing the generic registration form with a specific job title, actual student request, job specifications, and benefits-focused copy. The variation increased tutor sign-ups by 15%, representing approximately 20,000 additional applications in the first year. The insight came from traffic analysis showing that many visitors to the recruitment page arrived directly from job-search sites, meaning they were job-hunting rather than looking to join a platform. The change reframed the page from "register with us" to "apply for this real job," using language and specifics that matched visitor intent. This illustrates a supply-side optimization principle: in a two-sided marketplace, tutor acquisition is often as constraining as student acquisition, yet receives less attention and optimization effort.
strategic_hook: Understanding the two-sided nature of marketplace business models reveals that supply-side customer acquisition and conversion can be the binding constraint on growth, requiring distinct strategy and messaging tailored to supplier needs and job-search behavior.

heading: THE IMPACT OF CONTENT FRESHNESS ON AI CITATIONS (9 MINUTE READ)
summary: AI assistants cite content averaging 25.7% fresher than organic Google results, with roughly half of all AI citations coming from content updated within the last 13 weeks. However, this freshness advantage decays quickly—the median citation half-life across platforms is about 4.5 weeks, meaning visibility must be continuously re-earned rather than locked in. Different AI platforms weight freshness differently: Perplexity and Grok favor it most heavily (freshness scores 85–87), ChatGPT aggressively prioritizes new content (393–458 days newer than organic baseline), while Google's AI Overviews actually cite slightly older content (-16 days). Updating publish dates without substantive content changes doesn't work; real refreshes require adding new statistics, current data, or updated sections, with research showing that adding statistics can lift citations by up to 37%. The strategic response is a tiered refresh cadence—weekly for top-traffic pages, monthly for high-value content, quarterly for pillars—that distinguishes between content decay (competing against newer sources) and semantic drift (terminology or framing falling out of step with current discussion).
strategic_hook: A customer strategy team should map which AI platforms their target customers use most heavily to determine whether a freshness-first cadence or a quality-first approach better serves that segment's actual search behavior and expectations.

heading: CAPTURE ATTENTION THAT LASTS WITH 15-SECOND ENGAGED VIDEO VIEWS (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: Reddit has launched 15-second Engaged Video Views, a new advertising optimization goal and billing model available in public beta globally. The feature targets Reddit users most likely to watch videos to completion or for at least 15 seconds, and advertisers pay only for these meaningful views. Alpha testers reported significant performance improvements, including a 51% increase in 15-second view-through rates and a 71% increase in video completion rates on average. The tool is designed for longer-form creative that requires more time to convey its message, such as product demos, trailers, testimonials, and feature explainers, and includes automated bidding options to reduce manual campaign management. Reddit recommends using 15-second views for stories that build over time and 6-second views for messages that land immediately. Advertisers can test the new goal against the existing 6-second optimization through Reddit's Split Testing feature, which allows controlled experiments to measure performance differences.
strategic_hook: Advertisers evaluating which video formats and messaging approaches drive customer consideration should use Reddit's Split Testing capability to understand whether their target audience requires longer engagement time, directly informing creative strategy and messaging architecture decisions.

heading: BUILD VS. BUY: MARKETING TOOLS IN THE VIBE CODE ERA (6 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article presents a framework for marketing teams deciding whether to build internal tools using AI or buy existing software solutions. Authors Sarah and Matt evaluate eight marketing technology categories—CRM, CMS, audience data platforms, BI tools, email systems, SEO tracking, A/B testing, and attribution—and separately recommend build or buy for each, finding surprising agreement. Their core insight is that build decisions make sense for tools handling data that companies already own (audience data, attribution, dashboards, website content), while buy decisions apply to categories requiring hard infrastructure work like deliverability, compliance, crawler fleets, and API integrations. The article provides practical vendor-evaluation questions, including whether cancellation would cause real pain, whether the product's value lies in the data customers have entered, and whether API access would enable custom LLM workflows.
strategic_hook: Teams should map their existing marketing technology stack against the build/buy framework to identify which categories represent genuine competitive advantages versus commodity infrastructure, informing both vendor renewal decisions and resource allocation for internal tool development.

heading: CREATORS AS A SALES ENGINE: HOW CHINA IS RETHINKING THE ENTIRE CUSTOMER JOURNEY (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: China's social commerce ecosystem demonstrates how creators function as integrated sales infrastructure rather than mere marketing channels, with platforms like Rednote combining content discovery, creator feeds, search, livestreaming, and e-commerce into a single customer journey. The article illustrates this through Mr. Wang's laundry detergent purchase: he discovers the product through creator content on Rednote, gets retargeted with aligned videos from different creators, watches livestream shopping events, and completes his purchase directly within the platform. China's livestream commerce market reached $900 billion in 2025, with leading hosts generating up to roughly €800 million in single-day sales, encouraging diverse participation from celebrities and retail staff. The shift reflects a move away from traditional advertising toward creator-driven, trust-based communication, as platforms integrate e-commerce functions directly into their ecosystems and brands redirect investment from centrally produced content toward KOL-created material. While European ecosystems remain fragmented across search engines, retailers, and social platforms, the trajectory is clear: as TikTok and similar platforms expand to include shopping features, social networks are increasingly covering more steps of the customer journey, requiring brands to rethink their starting point from format-based to consumer-journey-based.
strategic_hook: Brands need to map how their customer journeys are shifting across platforms and understand where creators now control consumer access and trust before determining media investment and content strategy.

heading: STICKI ROLLS IS TURNING STICKERS INTO THE NEW SOCIAL CURRENCY (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: Sticki Rolls, a collectible sticker brand founded by Josh Loerzel and Lev Nelson, has become a Gen Alpha cultural phenomenon by combining shareability and self-expression with creator partnerships. The brand surpassed 1 billion YouTube views and 1.9 million subscribers by prioritizing organic growth during the 2024 unboxing wave, while partnering with Kawaii artists Anna Altamirano and Erin Degan. In August 2026, Sticki Rolls hosted a pop-up collaboration with Chillhouse nail salon in Soho that attracted nearly 1,000 guests over two days, with 500 participating in complimentary sticker manicures and experiencing new collectibles like Sticki Mates bag charms. The event generated significant digital lift, driving Google search interest up 50% week-over-week and 130% month-over-month, while adding over 20,000 new YouTube subscribers. The success validated bringing Sticki Rolls' tactile, community-driven experience from wholesale into immersive brick-and-mortar spaces, with leadership considering a potential pop-up roadshow to other cities based on fan demand captured via social media comments.
strategic_hook: Understanding the multi-generational household consumption pattern for Gen Alpha products—where parents co-consume with children—directly informs customer journey mapping and market positioning for brands targeting this demographic.

heading: SKIMS MARKETING STRATEGY: KIM KARDASHIAN'S BILLION-DOLLAR BRAND (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: SKIMS, founded by Kim Kardashian in September 2019, became a billion-dollar brand not through celebrity cachet alone but by repositioning shapewear from a shame-based hidden undergarment into visible lifestyle wear through inclusive product design (9 nude shades, XXS to 5X sizing) and strategic marketing. The company targets Gen Z and Millennial women aged 18-34, who comprise 70% of revenue, and is expanding into men's athletic wear through NBA partnerships. SKIMS leverages five key strategies: Kim's 344 million Instagram followers as owned distribution infrastructure, artificial scarcity through limited drops that create urgency and eliminate discounting, high-profile partnerships with brands like Nike and the WNBA to borrow credibility across unrelated categories, grassroots micro-influencer seeding across diverse body types for authentic user-generated content, and disciplined owned-channel marketing with approximately five emails per week driving repeat engagement. The brand's success demonstrates that category redefinition combined with genuine product-market fit, owned distribution, and retention math outweighs the hype typically associated with celebrity brands.
strategic_hook: SKIMS' market analysis identified a structural gap in the shapewear category where consumer needs (inclusive sizing, body positivity, visible styling) were unmet by incumbents, enabling a complete category repositioning that should inform how businesses research and understand underserved customer segments before entering competitive markets.

heading: TIKTOK COMMENTS ARE GETTING MORE INTERACTIVE WITH VOICE COMMENTS, POLLS, AND MORE (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: TikTok is rolling out new interactive comment features including voice comments (up to one minute long), polls for creators, photo carousel comments (up to nine photos), and Live Photo comments with motion previews. Voice comments are launching globally over the next month for users 18 and older and will be moderated using speech-to-text transcription combined with human and automated detection. Polls can include up to five options with customizable voting timeframes and are now available globally to creators commenting on their own videos. The company is borrowing features from messaging apps to transform comment sections from simple feedback areas into spaces where users linger and deeply engage with each other, mirroring TikTok's historical strength in audio and music-driven trends.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: DUSTED (WEBSITE)
summary: Dusted is a community-driven platform where marketers publish and discover case studies to build credibility and demonstrate real-world marketing expertise beyond traditional resumes. The platform organizes case studies by discipline (product marketing, growth marketing, sales enablement, etc.) and by business outcomes (build GTM strategy, conduct customer research, launch a product, increase adoption). Featured case studies include efforts like building AI agents to automate cross-functional updates, creating 3D interactive sales platforms, executing multi-product GTM launches, and establishing organic marketing engines. High-performing case studies earn engagement metrics; for example, Emily Pick's study on turning a stalling upsell product into a 40% lift garnered 661k impressions and a 46% engagement rate. Key insights aggregated across the platform show trends including Claude Projects becoming an output driver for product launches, rising AI adoption in customer research, declining gated content in favor of open access, and onboarding emerging as a key driver for expansion revenue.
strategic_hook: Dusted enables customer strategy professionals to conduct competitive and market analysis by studying real case studies that reveal how peer companies identified customer needs, segmented audiences, built positioning strategies, and executed go-to-market plans across different industries and business models.

heading: SHOULD THERE BE AEO AGENCIES? (6 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article argues that traditional SEO agencies have become obsolete because their core deliverable—content production—can now be replicated by AI tools like Claude at a fraction of the cost, with the author noting that most agencies have simply rebranded their content teams as "AEO specialists" without fundamentally changing their work. The author contends that agencies survived historically by selling measurable but superficial deliverables like blog posts and ranking dashboards, when the real value should have been strategy. To remain viable, agencies must pivot to two primary offerings: first, deep customer and product strategy work that understands jobs-to-be-done and competitive positioning in ways internal teams cannot execute alone, and second, genuine PR work that builds brand credibility with journalists and analysts—a critical asset now because AI language models cite sources with established third-party credibility. The future agency will be smaller, staffed primarily with strategists and PR professionals rather than writers, and will measure success by business growth and earned media outcomes rather than articles produced, billing more like a strategic consultancy than a content factory.
strategic_hook: Understanding customer needs and competitive market positioning through jobs-to-be-done analysis is positioned as the core strategic differentiator that agencies must provide to justify their continued existence, requiring customer research capabilities that most in-house teams lack.

heading: WHAT DRIVES GEN Z BRAND LOYALTY IN 2026? (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: Rival Technologies surveyed 903 Gen Z consumers in the US and Canada in July-August 2026 to understand brand loyalty drivers, challenging the narrative that Gen Z is inherently disloyal. The research found that 64% of Gen Z stay loyal "always" or "most of the time," but only 11% feel brands understand them "really well"—and among that small group, 45% are loyal "always" versus just 5% among those who feel misunderstood, a nine-fold difference. Price and value (82%) and product quality (80%) dominate loyalty drivers, far outweighing values-alignment (36%) and influencer recommendations (9%). The study also revealed meaningful geographic and age-based segmentation: US Gen Z are nearly three times more likely than Canadian Gen Z to feel understood by brands, and customer service importance climbs from 22% among the youngest (18-20) to 38% among older Gen Z (25-29). Marketers are urged to prioritize product fundamentals first, then invest in personalization and relevance to make Gen Z feel understood, treating values-alignment as a loyalty multiplier rather than a substitute for core product delivery.
strategic_hook: Companies developing Gen Z customer acquisition and retention strategies should use these segmentation insights—geographic differences and age-cohort loyalty drivers—to tailor their go-to-market approach rather than applying a single North American Gen Z campaign.

heading: HOW TO HANDLE NEGATIVE COMMENTS ON REDDIT (WHEN THE CRITICISM IS ALREADY RANKING) (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: Negative comments on Reddit are increasingly visible in Google search results and AI assistant responses, making them a critical touchpoint for prospective customers evaluating brands. Rather than attempting suppression through moderation, the article recommends community management: selectively engaging with negative threads as a named human representative, offering genuine help where possible, and leaving most criticism unanswered. The approach relies on four principles—show work, praise often, teach first, and stay firm—combined with the REACT framework (review user history, evaluate comment nature, assess willingness to engage, consider time frame, take thoughtful action) to distinguish between frustrated customers and bad-faith actors. Recent data suggests positive and negative Reddit threads now achieve comparable upvote visibility, meaning well-pitched contributions can reach audiences as effectively as complaints. Success is measured not by immediate sentiment improvements but by whether high-ranking threads contain accurate information, moderator relationships remain functional, and myths get corrected organically over time.
strategic_hook: Understanding how and where customers encounter your brand's reputation online—particularly on owned and unowned platforms that rank in search—is essential for mapping the customer journey and identifying where intervention in community spaces can shift perception at scale.

heading: YOUR PUBLIC BOOKING FORM IS A BOT MAGNET. HERE IS HOW TO SEAL IT (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: The author discovered that DraftKit's public booking forms were receiving spam submissions from bots within three weeks of launch, with suspicious patterns including addresses ending in .ru, placeholder text, and fake Substack URLs. Upon investigation, she found that AI builders like Lovable generate functional form components without bot protection mechanisms, creating an exposure that goes undetected until users complain. Cloudflare Radar data shows bots now generate the majority of web traffic, making public forms accepting name, email, and message fields particularly vulnerable. The author recommends adding Cloudflare Turnstile before launch (free up to one million monthly requests), verifying tokens server-side in edge functions before database insertion, implementing database-level validation triggers, logging failed bot checks, and auditing all public endpoints before shipping. This matters because most SaaS products only add bot protection after customer complaints rather than before launch, resulting in both cleanup costs and trust damage that could have been avoided with 30 minutes of preventive work.
strategic_hook: Product teams should audit all customer-facing public endpoints for bot vulnerability before launch as part of understanding the full customer journey and potential friction points, and model threat scenarios for any form accepting direct user input before marketing acquisition channels drive traffic.

heading: BECOME A MARKETING ENGINEER (WEBINAR)
summary: Maven is offering a free 30-minute webinar introducing the Marketing Engineer role, an emerging position that combines marketing knowledge with systems thinking to identify and build automated marketing workflows. The role is highly coveted in the US, commanding salaries between $150,000 and $300,000 for candidates with just a few years of experience. Instructors Dino Myers-Lamptey (voted Top 10 UK Media Planner six times) and Lee Henshaw (30+ years in marketing and technology) teach participants how to build marketing automation using no-code platforms like n8n, demonstrating an AI Focus Group Agent that conducts synthetic market research. The webinar covers why marketing teams need to build automation rather than buy it, how to develop the systems thinking needed for the role, and includes upcoming workshops on becoming a marketing engineer.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: TIKTOK JUST MADE PAID SOCIAL AGENTIC (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: TikTok has launched Ads MCP and Agentic Hub, enabling AI agents to connect directly to TikTok Ads and manage campaigns, analyze performance, and handle creative and audience workflows without requiring marketers to switch between tools. Beyond the technical connector, TikTok is building an ecosystem of reusable "Skills"—packaged methodologies and processes for specific advertising tasks like creative fatigue analysis, budget optimization, and reporting that teams can employ within supported AI environments. The article distinguishes between repeatable workflows where AI can operate independently (reporting, QA, anomaly detection) and decisions requiring human judgment (strategic interpretation and business context). As agentic capabilities become standardized across platforms, competitive advantage will shift from platform access to how well teams encode their proprietary methodologies, decision frameworks, and guardrails into AI workflows. The implication for paid social teams is a shift in operating model: capturing institutional expertise as reusable systems while freeing practitioner capacity to focus on strategy, creative development, and connecting performance to business outcomes.
strategic_hook: Organizations can use agentic AI adoption as an opportunity to conduct customer strategy work by mapping their best-performing decision-making processes and performance evaluation frameworks, then codifying those insights into AI-driven workflows that reflect their unique understanding of customer needs and market positioning.

heading: REDDIT MAX CAMPAIGNS ARE NOW AVAILABLE TO ALL ADVERTISERS (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: Reddit has expanded its Max campaigns automation tool to all advertisers after a successful beta launch. Max campaigns automate targeting, creative selection, placement, and budget allocation while maintaining advertiser control, and beta testing showed 17% lower costs per acquisition and over 27% more conversions compared to standard campaigns. The platform announced three updates: Advertising API support for third-party integration, a new Smartly partnership as the first supported platform, and asset groups that allow advertisers to organize multiple creative sets by product line within a single campaign. Reddit platforms hosts 26 billion conversations and delivers 2.1x higher incremental return on ad spend than the digital media average. Case studies show strong results, including Fender achieving 148% ROAS with 126% higher click-through rate during Black Friday and LensDirect reaching 5.5x overall ROAS with evergreen campaigns.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: GLOSSIER AND DISHOOM'S ROYA SHARIAT ON BUILDING BRANDS, FOLLOWING YOUR CURIOSITY, AND DESIGNING AN UNCONVENTIONAL CAREER (6 MINUTE READ)
summary: Roya Shariat, who spent 6.5 years leading brand work at Glossier before moving to London to head brand and communications at restaurant chain Dishoom, shares insights on her unconventional career trajectory and brand-building philosophy. She landed her first Glossier role by pitching founder Emily Weiss on the street with a data-backed five-slide presentation about social impact, demonstrating that customer research showed consumers increasingly make value-led purchasing choices. At Dishoom, she emphasizes that in service businesses the brand experience is delivered through staff—requiring leadership to bring hospitality teams along as "first customers"—and that the founders' principle of "deepen, don't dilute" maintains brand authenticity during expansion by prioritizing awesome food, service, and team happiness over profit maximization. She credits Emily Weiss with teaching her deep customer devotion and continuous improvement, and Dishoom founder Shamil Thakrar with demonstrating that successful brands need "a little poetry at the heart of it." Her broader advice for aspiring brand marketers emphasizes talking to many people to maximize "surface area for luck," authenticity in interviews, and the willingness to try imperfect work rather than being paralyzed by analysis.
strategic_hook: Roya's approach to pitching the Glossier social impact role demonstrates how customer research and competitive insight—specifically data showing value-driven consumer purchasing behavior and employee expectations—can build a business case for a new strategic initiative aligned with brand positioning.

heading: GOOGLE'S LATEST STUDY REVEALS HOW LLMS RECALL FACTS (6 MINUTE READ)
summary: Google Research found that advanced AI models store 95–98% of facts from their training data but fail to directly recall 26–34% of them, a problem only partially mitigated by enabling thinking mode, which still misses 11–12%. The recall failures occur primarily through two mechanisms: the "reversal curse," where models struggle when questions flip a fact's direction from how it was learned, and fact rarity, where less common information is harder to retrieve. Marketers cannot control how LLMs evolve or how customers phrase queries, but can optimize their own content to improve AI recall of key business facts. The article recommends three tactics: state marketing messages in multiple directions to address the reversal curse, audit AI visibility using tools like OmniSEO to identify which brand facts appear in AI-powered search results, and turn audit findings into a content action plan by placing USPs across multiple pages and formats to make them "popular" facts that LLMs can more reliably retrieve.
strategic_hook: Understanding how LLMs retrieve information about competitors versus your own business should inform competitive analysis and content strategy, as it reveals whether visibility gaps stem from missing content versus retrieval failures that require different solutions.

heading: INFLUENCERS MOSTLY SKIP DISCLOSURE (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: A massive industry of 26.6 million U.S. influencers operates with inconsistent disclosure rules because neither the FTC nor E.U. regulators legally define "influencer," instead using terms like "endorser" and "trader." In a February 2024 sweep of 576 E.U. influencers, 97 percent posted commercial content but only 20 percent disclosed it systematically, and only 36 percent of those conducting commercial activity were registered as traders. The U.S. FTC requires disclosure of any "material connection" (payment, free products, discounts, or employment ties) with no minimum threshold, while the E.U. mandates platform-provided ad-flagging and deepfake labeling, with France and Germany imposing additional thresholds and levies. Enforcement varies: U.S. penalties cap at $53,088 per FTC violation plus state class actions, E.U. fines reach 4 percent of turnover or €2 million, and France adds criminal exposure. Notable cases include the 2016 Lord & Taylor settlement over undisclosed Instagram posts reaching 11.4 million people and Kim Kardashian's $1.26 million SEC fine for a concealed crypto promotion, with new state-level class actions naming both brands and influencers as co-defendants.
strategic_hook: Understanding influencer disclosure requirements and enforcement landscapes is critical for developing customer-acquisition strategies that comply with regulations across U.S. and E.U. markets and avoid legal exposure that damages brand trust.
